standard_prerequisites.name: Separatedness and uniqueness of limits / specialization lifting
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Schemes (separated morphisms and specialization to a point)
standard_prerequisites.use: Used to conclude x = x' once their generic specializations agree over the same point of Y.

core_obligations: For two points x, x' with a common image y, pick a specialization y_0 -> y where y_0 is a generic point of an irreducible component of Y (proof lines 8904-8905).

Since f is locally an isomorphism, lift the specialization to specializations x_0 -> x and x'_0 -> x' mapping to y_0 -> y; observe x_0, x'_0 are generic points of components of X and hence equal by hypothesis (3) (proof lines 8906-8908).
Use separatedness of f to conclude x = x'; with f locally an open immersion and injective, conclude f is an open immersion (proof lines 8908-8909).
proof_roadmap: Reduce injectivity of f to comparing two lifts of a specialization of a generic point of Y.
Lift the specialization through the local isomorphisms and identify the two generic points over y_0.
Apply separatedness to deduce the two points coincide, making f injective and hence an open immersion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes open immersions among separated morphisms that are open immersions on an open covering and whose restriction to the generic points of the irreducible components of the source is injective. The proof specializes: two points x, x' with a common image y are pushed up from a specialization y_0 -> y of a generic point of a component of Y to specializations x_0 -> x, x'_0 -> x'; the generic points coincide by hypothesis, and separatedness identifies x = x' (proof lines 8904-8909). H2: the simultaneous lifting of specializations and the use of separatedness to compare the two lifts is the non-routine step.
